title: Edge of Eternities: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: "You again?"
An intelligent jetpack for those who find themselves lost in space.
"Stygian demon! You are sentenced to ten cycles of illumination. May the light scour the shadow from your soul."
As the supervoid's photon collar washed over them, time stopped. Their souls would experience the grandeur of their demise for eternity.
"My purpose is my spear. My spear is my life. My life is for the Regent Maximum."
Cosmogrands of the Celestial Palatinate always seek to expand their grip on the Edge.
"Arrive as the dawn, and banish night through your brilliance!"
Eternity columns are the trade hubs of every solar system.
"You fight beside me as brilliantly as the dawn. I have nothing more to teach you." —Master Iridiss
"Haste begets blunder. Be patient, Aora. As the sun rises, you will yet earn your second blade." —Master Iridiss
"This is your captain speaking. Our eternity drive has ruptured. Light be with you all."
"An Astelli once saved me just like this. I aspire to live up to their example every day."
The hidden might of the Sunstar Free Company is its technical staff.
"We are the arrows of Sunsolde's Quiver." —*Declaration of Fleet Purpose*, Axiom 2
"I have forgotten sleep in their prison." —Korelaa, prison escapee
"With this mantle, you carry the duty to spread light, liberty, and the grace of Taman IV to the stars."
"Hope can never fade so long as there's a hand to carry my sword when I fall."
"I thank you that I do not shine alone."
Born of dead stars, the Astelli may fight for light, but they know the void as their womb.
"Only when a vessel is emptied of shallow ego may the depths of light flow in to fill it." —Seraphus Chek, Sunstar poet
"The light does not ask permission to cut through the darkness." —Mentor Ultimate, to Regent Maximum Taman IV
"We've received transmission! They're alive—just barely." —Sunstar Free Company Mission Control
Drix hunt down Eldrazi Potentiate without hesitation or explanation.
"Brightstar-1 to FlightComm: Scopes are clear. The stars are yours."
"You are a suspect in an ongoing investigation. Do not resist apprehension."
She forges blades of incandescence and quenches them in pitch darkness.
His people watched the Eldrazi rise and the Fomori fall. Never will they watch again.
The Sunstar Free Company is not swayed by profit. Sunstar is their faith, the prism through which they cast light across Sothera.
"Your ship and crew have been contaminated by the great destroyers. We cannot risk their spread. Prepare for unraveling."
When packing for a stealth mission, it's important to fold your dimensions tightly.
All Uthros networks are routed through an ancient relic called a memory vessel, which converts data into thought.
A cloudsculptor at work is like a carefully balanced weather system, and just as dangerous to interfere with.
Even across the Edge, a dog is still a dog.
Older than the Eumidian seedships that populated Evendo.
Illvoi are masters of the deep freeze, though conditions must be perfect to avoid going to pieces.
"Your atoms will serve my ambitions in a much more useful form."
Illvoi hope for the best outcomes but engineer for the worst.
Emissary mechans are often assigned their own security detail given their importance in inter-Pinnacle dialogs.
The shadow of the godcore falls over Uthros, and the world erupts with storms.
Uthros guards have such rapid reflexes that it has led to rumors of experimental precognition.
Cloudkill agents slip in and out like a breeze.
The Uthros Combine's first question for any scientific breakthrough is always: "How can this be used to keep our next breakthrough secret?"
Every so often, the Edge reminds you that there's always more to discover.
Every iteration brings it closer to understanding its own creation.
Illvoi temper their curiosity with caution, deploying mechan pilots before they risk mortal scientists.
"Do not mistake a preference for peace for an inability to fight." —Yvin, Pinnacle envoy
Illvoi nervous systems are decentralized. Even as one part runs calculations, another might contemplate the depths of Uthros.
Cloudsculpting naturally led the Illvoi to other methods of reshaping matter.
The Illvoi hunt for stellar fragments that predate even the Fomori.
Sometimes the best parts are already in use.
It harnesses energy from the brutal, mana-rich storms found deep within Uthros.
Drix weftwalking requires neither eternity columns nor Pinnacle codebooks. But the art is ancient, and each passing is a leap of faith.

"Log entry cycle 33,507: Tenuous perception of psionic activity emanating from Uthros's core. Nature: Nonlinguistic, fragmentary. Content: Isolation, apoplexy. It wants free." —Uthros Combine research notes
"All things end. I'd rather embrace that truth than the fantasy of eternal light."
The Kav had learned their lesson about mining too deep. Zern Miffles had not.
The Eumidians sought the secret of weftwalking in Drix DNA. Though they failed, their attempts yielded other gains.
"Found the stranded crew in an icy labyrinth. Well, what's left of them." —Decrypted log 2.23
One last chance. Make it count.
"You would kill the Faller—our messiah—and call *us* monsters?"
The Sunstar faith teaches of Perfect Void—of emptying oneself so that the light may fill the hollow. But in the void of death, its teachings bring little comfort.
It's an acquired taste.
"Join me in the Next Eternity."
"Death is a trick of the light. Snuff it out and discover immortality." —Plummet Record 170.312
It's difficult to dodge a weapon that commands gravity itself.

"Sing! When the Faller reaches the end of his journey, all things will arrive at the Zero Point. What is unending will persist through to the new creation and be ordered accordingly." —*The Theorem Unending and Final,* Antiphon 6
Her food stores will run out before her fuel, leaving only her mechan gravpack to carry her remains to the Next Eternity.
"Sunstar thinking is too linear. While they fight head-on, we hit them everywhere else." —Alpharael, Stonechosen
"Does truth lie in the void between stanzas?"
"Redd's gone. And the chittering—it won't stop!" —Decrypted log 3.88
"You have been given great purpose. Your matter will feed the singularity."
It does to ships what the Monoist faith does to stars.
Monoists fight a war of attrition, knowing their victory is inevitable so long as they stay true to their faith.
The swarm lacked a natural predator, so the Eumidians became one.
It will not end any other way than this.
"Rejoice, and know all will join you soon." —Calnan, Monoist assassin
The Eumidian biotechs were delighted when a mutated malware gene devastated their systems. They'd encourage the trait, so long as future clutches could be contained.
The voidforged lack the formal programming of other mechan. Instead, they are engineered to move in accordance with the hymn of the Immortal Faller.
Democracy is not always just.
"They will call you a monster, but I call you worthy."
"Beyond the supervoid, existence collapses into a singular point. We are all dead. We all live." —Xu-Ifit, osteoharmonist
"Go back to your little war, sun-stooge! This here is *our* operation!" —Kunthaar, Kav mine operator
When fighting Kav, always expect each action to have an unequal and opposite overreaction.
"Adapt to this, you bug-eyed planet-squatters!" —Admiral Scargruf, Kavaron Memorial Navy
The rapacious appetite that ended their world became the only means by which the Kav could lift their civilization from it.
The Kav have more than ideology or profit on the line. They fight for a home.
The mining gear that crumbled their planet could also deal terrible damage to flesh.
"It saves a lot on ammunition. No, I'm not kidding." —Captain Mayav, Kavaron Memorial Navy
Once the security for a moxite mine, now a ghost in a hollowed-out cavern.
Scavengers looking to steal from Kav mining sites rarely make that mistake again.
"Safe? Buddy, the whole planet is falling apart, we don't have time for safe." —Dorgan, Kav roboticist
A Kav landing —Sotheran expression meaning "a bad time"
Only the most skilled matter shapers can imbue moxite with other raw energies, but the rewards are well worth the dangers.
Recover the treasures in Kavaron's memorial vaults—by any means necessary.
"Let's show those bugs our own style of splicin'."
Legend says the first Regent Maximum was herself a dragon. She illuminated the void and gifted the Celestial Palatinate lightforging.
The Kav pilot gleefully ignored his lander's collision warning.
It wasn't the most efficient design, but the miners refused to part with "Ol' Pangy."
Excess energy from the moxite core is focused into a destructive ray of plasma.
While the Kavaron tiger has been extinct for centuries, its renowned ferocity endures.
Even until Exodus Day, those in power on Kavaron refused to acknowledge that the planet was trying to tell them something.
"We build our beamcutters to mince bedrock. Should slice a Eumidian hull with no issues."
Kav battle rhetoric teaches that there are no malfunctions on the battlefield, just equipment that need to be utilized differently.
It scrounges Kavaron's wasteland, unaware that its home can no longer support its purpose.
"Who cares if it rips the asteroid apart? We got what we needed." —Viya, Kav moxite baron
"We're a few bones short of a skeleton crew, Sami, but we've got plenty of spine."
A victory was the best retirement gift the admiral could have asked for.
"Your land, or my blades."
Some creatures have adapted to thrive in the unstable chaos of Kavaron That Is.
"Give everything and advance!" —Kav naval motto
"Soon we'll have enough firepower to rid Evendo of its bug infestation." —General Tekvu, Kavaron Memorial Navy
Infinite Guideline's "Fauna from Sothera" exhibit proved popular. Unfortunately, the biological zookeepers kept getting eaten.
Maybe in your next evolution. —Eumidian insult
Death never smelled so sweet.
Many mistake terrasymbiotic philosophy as pacifism. They are rarely wrong twice.
"We will not yield until the Eumidians relinquish our Kavaron Tomorrow." —Official Kav diplomatic statement
Charting the Edge, one scan at a time.
To plant the seeds of the other is to cultivate the self. —Eumidian aphorism
A harmonious production for a better world.
Not all species on Evendo welcomed the thawing of the ice.
When falling shards of Kavaron shattered the icy shell of Evendo, the Eumidian seed pods were far from the only form of life awakened from slumber.
Most say the Edge cannot be measured, but some will spend their lives trying anyway.
Eumidians have engineered a device or species to manage every stage of terrasymbiosis.
Beyond the borders of Pinnacle space, alien worlds of untold wonder await.
By stimulating violent behavior in its host, the mite scavenges the remains of prey much too large for it to hunt on its own.
As warmth crept across Evendo, many long-dormant species grew bolder.
"Come! Join me in the sun!"
Narix felt their molt coming. Before taking a new form, they had to find what Evendo required of them.
"Oh, look at the size of those petals! That one's eaten well this season." —Bez, Pinnacle nature surveyor
There are no failures in terrasymbiosis, only lessons learned.
Meltstriders are the bleeding edge of Evendo's frontier thaw.
"I've found a strange vine in the ice. Thawing for further analysis." —Meltstrider log, final entry
Tannuk's gut warned of danger, but Sami forged ahead without heed.
Knowledge isn't found, but grown.
A new brood finds its home on the doorstep of another's.
The Eumidians sought to keep Evendo a gentle world—at any cost.
Eumidian thermal wands protect their new home as well as thaw it.
Drix never leave their worlds defenseless.
For Eumidians, terraforming and evolution are one and the same. They grow as their planet grows, in lockstep coexistence.
"We are as ice," their mentor once told them, "Destined to shed our rigid form and nourish the grounds with our melting."
"I am worthy of the Faller's blessing. I can prove it."
"Life is a pattern, not a material."
"Modify these alleles and try again."
>Alert: COSMOGOYF >Recommended Action: RUN —PSS *Erix* shipboard computer, final transmission
"We can all be more than we are. Let me help."
"By the eternal and everflowing light, I swear myself to this cause."
"What crime did you commit that makes *me* your best option?" —Tezzeret
Kavaron's degradation poisoned many hearts, which the Monoists were happy to exploit.
Whenever Sami was down on their luck, they returned to an old comfort: the clinks and clanks of tinkering.
"The hard way it is."
"Inspiration blossoms from fertile rot."
The howling winds could hardly be heard over the maddening thoughts of the godcore.
"Keeping tabs on a whole station is too much for just one."
A new dawn, burning away the darkness.
Serving in the Memorial Navy was nothing like the posters made it out to be.
For navigating that which was, is, and will be.
The Edge is littered with the vestiges of civilizations annihilated by the Eldrazi.
Liberation Station's morale greatly improved after Rover took up residence.
The wastelands of yesterday's colonies will pave the road to tomorrow's.
"What flavor do you want, Sami? Bland, dense, or vanilla?" —Tannuk
A miniature star, replicating the mana-aether reactions in a sun's core.
"I'll never escape this rock, but I fear they will." —Decrypted log 4.11
Nano-infectant: A category-Phi substance, capable of infecting both organics and artificials. Weaponizing it is a war crime.
"Log 1.4.778: Granove, a tropical moon teeming with endemic biota. A must see for any aspiring astrobiologist!" —*Maisie's Edge Chronicles*
"Log 1.7.618: Starshadow, a relic of a culture lost to calamity. Its people were eradicated in a single day—but by what?" —*Maisie's Edge Chronicles*
"Log 2.2.119: Kiln, known for its blazing forges and ancient lava seeps. The footing may be treacherous, but the metallurgy is grand!" —*Maisie's Edge Chronicles*
The heat of a sun condensed into a forge.
"Log 2.5.325: A newborn moon, Aqqat still churns with the fires of creation. I'm eager to see what it will become!" —*Maisie's Edge Chronicles*
"Log 2.9.089: Lammuat, the cemetery moon of salvage and secrets. Could be profitable for those brave enough to plumb its recesses." —*Maisie's Edge Chronicles*
Beyond the edge of faith lies eternal hope.
Those lucky enough to survive leave with greater perspective of their own importance.
Beyond the the edge of devotion lies eternal ambition.
"Tear away the rotten flesh of 'reality' and behold the pristine bones of Truth."
In desperate times, Kavaron's greatest minds strive to elevate their civilization.
Beyond the edge of doubt lies eternal loyalty.
"Some things are bigger than one's self."
Beyond the edge of desperation lies eternal ingenuity.
At the end of all things, will you find redemption or rebirth?
"Perfection lies beyond ego. Only through service can you become complete."
Droplets from its breaching splash newborn stars across the void.
Life, in all its explosive emotion, is never shorter than when used as a weapon.
Flickering through the space between chaos and weft, it glimpses cosmic truths.
It recycled malaise into exuberance.
A welcoming farewell to new neighbors.
Advancement is found in the collision of chaos and order.
To exist and be subject to its hunger are one and the same.
There is no blade sharper than betrayal.
More worlds have been forgotten than any living being could know.
Those who grasp for power might one day find it.
"All is the hand that weaves the Fabric of Being. The Fabric of Being is All." —*Drix Codex*, line 1
"Lightsick fools. All suns eventually set."
Kavaron cannot be saved, but its culture can.
The agony that consumed him also gave him clarity of purpose.
The future is set. The present remains uncertain.
"All things will fall to the Zero Point. By accepting this truth, my path is known and my fate is certain."
"That which should not have happened is undone, and a new pattern takes its place."
"Rejoice! For within sekhar, the final sacrifice, you will find passage to the Next Eternity." —Calnan, Monoist assassin
